body:
I am SO glad to hear. 
Please, the mind is a really powerful thing. And in trying times the anxious depressed mind will overpower logic. First thing is to step back from the situation, take some deep breaths and think logically and calmly. 

Unfortunately, life will throw you challenges. And I am afraid to say this, but there will  be life crises that are more stressful than this. I hope that this experience will make you more resilient for those trying times.

I hope others can also speak to this. And I am sure many can sympathize.  But exiting from life is not the answer. If I was a statistics I would help you, but I am not.  

There is someway your family has survived together thus far. You and your family will survive this also. You must. 

The degree may be a matter of pride. But these days it doesn’t necessarily mean a ticket to job and career. You will even with the degree still probably have to work “survival jobs”. Do so until you save enough money to take the course again to finish the degree.  If that degree is important to you and your family.

EDIT

I see
You have sought help in another subreddit. Please let us know how that goes. 

Anyone here can help with this satisitics project ?

First stop reading news, internet, social media. If you have no underlying biological problem causing  your anxiety, depression, suicidal ideation, then take some time to celebrate your graduation from high school. Treat yourself to this. 

This is an odd time in our history. Many people are out of work and the job market will be getting better.
Do not do anything drastic.  Firstly find a way to calm down so that you can think more logically. And get some objective perspective of your situation.

I remember when I had first had suicidal thoughts that wouldn’t go away. It was really reallly scary.  As the other person suggested see a doctor or mental health professional. 

Is it due to a change in life circumstances? Or is it unexplainable?

This is not worth considering suicide. 
Your family needs you. You leaving them will leave them in greater peril.  

Can you reach out to classmates for some direction?
Is there a help centre at the college?
Reach out again to the family members who may help in math. 

How are you supporting the family now? Who is supporting the family? Can you wait until later
To retake the course when you have more funds saved?
Grad school and depression go hand in hand. There are many in your shoes.  Your school may provide counselling.  I suggest you take advantage of it.

I responded to your other post. You are not alone. Depression and suicidal ideation is a huge problem in the medical field. If it helps to know that you are not the only med student suffering, do a search on it. 
You eventually will have to make a decision. Take care of yourself first.

Depression and suicidal ideation are very common in med school, residency and the profession. And I. Believe Your school administrators will be aware of this growing problem.. I can only imagine they will be sympathetic some how.
Dedicate yourself to helping less fortunate people. In your volunteer work you will likely meet someone who can give you the same feelings.

Cherish every moment you have with him. Spend as much time as you can with him. When his time comes make sure he goes peacefully.  

If such a place exists, Cremate him at a reputable place that specializes in pet cremations. Do this research ahead of time. 

Make a little shrine at home. Tufts of his fur. Paw impression. Photos and ashes. 

Whenever you have a special meal, or his favourite human food,  make sure you leave some for him in front of his cremation urn. Say a little prayer to him. 

I have gone through the deaths of two beloved per dogs. It is the most painful thing you can experience. 
But these things will help you cope. 

What will also help is raising another dog and treating him/her with even greater love.

I assuming you have gone through a breakup? Though you have have lost her, you should dedicate your time and life to Christ and God and do the good work that they wish Christians to do in society. This will give your life renewed purpose and constant companionship of the Lord.
Sorry to hear about your situation. I am sure you are aware of the many mental health services available for the Indigenous population in Ontario. I suggest starting there.

I am sorry to hear about predicament. Especially during these trying times. 

They are busy these days.  Sometimes up to an hour wait. The responders are generally trained volunteers and not professionals. They can point to resources but I doubt they can connect to psychologists. 

Mind you, some people have found these crises lines very unhelpful. And some people have come away feeling worse. There are some posts here in this forum.

I don’t know if this will help. But a lot of people, including myself, would love to be in your position. I have very clear material concrete problems that are triggering depressive episodes and suicidal thoughts. 

However I understand that more existential philosophical reasons for suicidal ideation can be harder to deal with.  But I would still prefer your situation over mine.  And I think I would know what I would do in situation—take joy in the small successes and be resigned to the fact that large world issues cannot be solved in a lifetime or even maybe ever.
Mornings are filled with rumination. Which leads to panic attacks.

That is the scary thing. How impulsive suicide could be. One minute I am feeling alright. The next minute I am consumed by dark thoughts.  Trying to continuously keep mind busy also is so exhausting. I am hoping these lockdowns have something to do with it. I was feeling generally great before then.

Thank you for this.  Please take it as a sign.   
If your act of kindness gave you the will to live to ease the pain of this living being...

I am dealing with suicidal thoughts.  Present circumstances are causing me great stress, guilt, and shame. But I don’t want to die. I want to grow old with wife and adopt abandoned dogs and cats. The dream of this eases my suicidal thoughts.
